To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the cation permeabilities of proton-conducting membranes based on SPEEK are lower than that of a NafION reference membrane, that SA-PEEK has the highest cation permeability and that amphoteric SAMPEEK has a permeability of cations comparable with that of SAPEEK.
the cation permeabilities of proton-conducting, anion-conductive and ampholytic polymer membranes were investigated and that the cation permselectivities of the membranes were found to be very high.
the cation permeation in SPEEK, SA and SAM-PEEEK membranes is significantly lower than that in Nafion 115.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the design of membranes for the electrochemical separation of cations from aqueous solutions.
the development of a new generation of ion-conducting polymers with low cation permeability for use as membranes in fuel cells.
the development of new ion-conducting membranes for electrochemical applications with a reduced permeability for electrochemically active species.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the cation permeabilities of the membranes investigated are in the order of 10− 9 cm2 · min− .
the cation permeation through an ion-conducting membrane is mainly determined by the cross-linking density, and that the nature of the ionic groups plays a minor role.

the ion permeability is mainly determined by the ion conductivity, and the permeability of cations through the membranes can be reduced by increasing the ion conductivity, i.e. by decreasing the cross-linking and by increasing the ion content of the polymer.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
cationic membranes based on PEEK or PSU, grafted with ionic groups, have low cation permeability, which is comparable with or even lower than that of Nafion.
the cation permeation is strongly influenced by the polymer structure, and the highest permeability is found for the proton-conducting SPEEK membranes.
the cation permeation of the membranes investigated in the present work is strongly dependent on the polymer structure, the type of ionic groups, and the cross-linking density.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the cation permeabilities of proton-conducting, anionic and amphoteric polymer membranes can be decreased to values as low as the permeabilities of the reference membrane Nafion 112.
cation permeability can be reduced by cross-linking the polymer backbone and/or by introducing ionic groups that have a low affinity to the cations of interest, such as vanadium ions.

the cation permeation can be reduced to values as low as those reported for Nafion by the introduction of cross-links, which is a key feature for the application of these membranes as separators for electrochemical energy conversion devices.
